再一次，她发现自己仍然在长长的走廊里，离那张小玻璃桌很近。
“Now, I’ll manage better this time,” she said to herself, and began by taking the little golden key, and unlocking the door that led into the garden.
“这一次我要做得好一些了，”她自言自语道，然后拿起那枚小金钥匙，把通向花园的门打开。

Then she went to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and then—she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
然后她开始啃那块蘑菇（她把它夹在口袋里），直到自己大约有脚高；然后她沿着小走廊走过去；然后——她终于发现自己在美丽的花园里，在那些五彩斑斓的花丛和清凉的喷泉之间。

ch.zt: 第八章 · 王后的槌球场
p: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red.
一大丛玫瑰树矗立在花园入口处：树上的玫瑰花是白色的，但树上有三个园丁，正忙着给它们涂成红色。
Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, “Look out now, Five!
Alice 觉得这是一件非常奇怪的事情，她走近去想看看，正巧她一走近，就听见其中一个说：“五，当心啊！”
Don’t go splashing paint over me like that!”
不要像那样泼油漆在我身上！
“I couldn’t help it,” said Five, in a sulky tone; “Seven jogged my elbow.”
“我忍不住了，”五号不高兴地说；“七号推了我一把。”
On which Seven looked up and said, “That’s right, Five!
Seven抬头说道：“五说的对！”
Always lay the blame on others!”
总是把责任推给别人！
“You’d better not talk!” said Five.
“你最好不要说话！”五说。
“I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!”
“我听王后说，昨天你还该被砍头！”
“What for?” said the one who had spoken first.
“为什么？”第一个说话的人说。
“That’s none of your business, Two!” said Seven.
“那跟你不相干，二号！”七号说。
“Yes, it is his business!” said Five, “and I’ll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions.”
“是的，那是他的事！”五号说道，“我告诉他——他把洋葱换成葱头给厨子了。”

Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun “Well, of all the unjust things—” when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.
七撇下画笔，正要开口说“世上最不公平的事——”这时他眼见爱丽丝站在那里，正看着他们，不由得突然住口，其他人都也回头去看，都向她行了礼。
“Would you tell me,” said Alice, a little timidly, “why you are painting those roses?”
“你会告诉我，”小鹿斑比 timidly 少少胆怯地说，“你为什么把那些蔷薇涂成这样？”
Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two.
五和七没有说话，却看着二。

Two began in a low voice, “Why the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know.
Two 开始低声说，“你得知道，小姐，这本来应该是一棵红玫瑰树，我们不小心放了一棵白玫瑰树进去；如果女王发现了，我们都会被砍头的，你知道。”
So you see, Miss, we’re doing our best, afore she comes, to—” At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out “The Queen!
所以你看，Miss，我们最好在她来之前，尽力——”这时，Five，一直焦虑地望着花园，喊道：“女王！”
The Queen!” and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces.
“女王！”三个园丁立刻趴在地上。
There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.
一阵脚步声传来，爱丽丝四处张望，急切地想看看王后是谁。

First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did.
十名士兵扛着棍子先上场；这些士兵的形状都像三名园丁，长方形扁平的，手和脚在角上：接着是十名侍从；他们全身都镶满了钻石，像士兵一样成双成对。
After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts.
接着是王室的孩子们；他们共有十人，小宝贝们手拉手、蹦蹦跳跳地一路向前，成双成对地走着；他们身上都装饰着心形图案。

Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her.
接下来是宾客，大多是国王和皇后，其中她认出了白兔：它匆匆忙忙地说话，笑答一切所说的话，却没注意到她。
Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.
然后是红心侍从，手里拿着国王的王冠，放在血红色的天鹅绒垫子上；最后，这庄严的行列中，国王和王后出现了。

Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions; “and besides, what would be the use of a procession,” thought she, “if people had all to lie down upon their faces, so that they couldn’t see it?”
Alice 感到有点怀疑，是否该像三名园丁那样趴在地上，但她记不得曾经听说过在游行中这样的规矩；“而且，如果人们都趴在地上，那么他们就什么都看不见，”她想，“那游行还有什么用呢?”
So she stood still where she was, and waited.
于是她站在原地，等着。
When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely “Who is this?”
当行列来到爱丽丝面前，它们都停了下来，看着她，王后严厉地说：“这是谁？”
She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.
她对红心侍者说，侍者只是鞠躬微笑作为回答。
“Idiot!” said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on, “What’s your name, child?”
“混账！”女王不耐烦地甩了甩头，然后转过身对爱丽丝说：“孩子，你叫什么名字？”
“My name is Alice, so please your Majesty,” said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself, “Why, they’re only a pack of cards, after all.
“我的名字是爱丽丝，陛下，请您称呼我为爱丽丝吧，”爱丽丝非常有礼貌地说，但她自己心里想道：“不过，他们只是扑克牌罢了。”
I needn’t be afraid of them!”
我不用怕他们！

“And who are these?” said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rose-tree; for, you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.
“How should I know?” said Alice, surprised at her own courage.
“我怎么会知道？”爱丽丝惊讶地问，自己的勇气令她感到意外。
“It’s no business of mine.”
“这与我无关。”
The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, screamed “Off with her head!
王后气得脸都红了，瞪了她一眼，像野兽一样，尖叫道：“把她的头砍下来！
Off—”
哎哟——
“Nonsense!” said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.
“胡说八道！”爱丽丝大声而坚决地说道，王后沉默了。
The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said “Consider, my dear: she is only a child!”
国王伸手按在她的胳膊上，小心翼翼地说：“亲爱的，考虑一下：她只是一个孩子！”
The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave “Turn them over!”
王后转过身，生气地对小人国说：“把他们翻过来！”
The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.
小人国小心翼翼地翻转了他们，用一只脚。
“Get up!” said the Queen, in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.
“起来！”王后尖声喊道，三个园丁立刻跳了起来，开始向国王、王后、王室的孩子以及其他人鞠躬。
“Leave off that!” screamed the Queen.
“别这样！”王后尖叫道。
“You make me giddy.”
“你让我头晕。
And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on, “What have you been doing here?”
然后，她转向玫瑰树，说：“你们在这里做了什么？”
“May it please your Majesty,” said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke, “we were trying—”
“陛下，”二号小人国谦卑地说道，跪下身子说，“我们正在尝试——”
“I see!” said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses.
“明白了！”王后说，她一直在检查玫瑰。
“Off with their heads!” and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.
“把他们的头砍下来！” procession继续前进，三个士兵留在后面，执行不幸的园丁，他们跑向爱丽丝寻求保护。
“You shan’t be beheaded!” said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near.
你休想被砍头！”，爱丽丝说，她把它们放进旁边的一盆大花盆里。
The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.
三个士兵四处走动了一会儿，寻找他们，然后悄悄地跟上其他人。
“Are their heads off?” shouted the Queen.
“他们的脑袋掉了吗？”王后喊道。
“Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!” the soldiers shouted in reply.
他们的脑袋不见了，陛下！士兵们回道。
“That’s right!” shouted the Queen.
那对！王后喊道。
“Can you play croquet?”
你可以打槌球吗？
The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.
士兵们沉默着，看着爱丽丝，因为问题显然是问她的。
“Yes!” shouted Alice.
“是的！”爱丽丝喊道。
“Come on, then!” roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.
“走吧，走吧！”王后吼道，爱丽丝跟着队伍走，心里非常想知道接下来会发生什么事。
“It’s—it’s a very fine day!” said a timid voice at her side.
“啊，真是个好天气！”她身边怯生生的声音说道。
She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.
她正沿着白兔走着，白兔焦急地窥视着她的脸。
“Very,” said Alice: “—where’s the Duchess?”
“非常，”爱丽丝说：“——黛西夫人在哪里？”
“Hush!
嘘！
Hush!” said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone.
嘘！ ”那只兔子压低了声音，匆匆说道。
He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered “She’s under sentence of execution.”
他说话时紧张地回头张望，然后踮起脚尖，把嘴凑到她的耳边低声说：“她被判了死刑。”
“What for?” said Alice.
“为什么？”爱丽丝说。
“Did you say ‘What a pity!’?” the Rabbit asked.
“你说‘真可惜！’吗？”兔子问道。
“No, I didn’t,” said Alice: “I don’t think it’s at all a pity.
“不，我没有说，”爱丽丝说：“我不认为这是很可惜。”
I said ‘What for?’”
“我问的是‘为什么？’”
“She boxed the Queen’s ears—” the Rabbit began.
“她打了王后的耳光——”兔子开始说。
Alice gave a little scream of laughter.
爱丽丝尖叫了一声笑。
“Oh, hush!” the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone.
“嘘！别出声！”兔子用害怕的声音说。
“The Queen will hear you!
“王后会听到的！”
You see, she came rather late, and the Queen said—”
“你瞧，她来得比较晚，王后说——”

“Get to your places!” shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other; however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began.
“到你们的位置上去！”王后用雷鸣般的声音喊道，人们开始四散奔逃，撞到一起；不过，他们很快就安定下来，游戏开始了。

Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life; it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.
爱丽丝从未见过如此奇怪的槌球场地，简直像一条条的沟壑和隆起的土丘；球是活的刺猬，槌是活的火烈鸟，士兵们得弯曲身体，倒立着，才能通过拱门。

The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it would twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.
爱丽丝一开始遇到的最大困难是槌球的控制：她把槌球的身子夹在腋下，腿垂下来，但通常，她刚把槌球的脖子整理好，准备用它的头部敲刺猬时，槌球就会扭动自己，用一种困惑的表情看着她，爱丽丝忍不住笑出声来；当她把槌球的头部放好，准备再次开始时，槌球又很让人恼火地发现刺猬已经展开身子，正在爬行。

The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting “Off with his head!” or “Off with her head!” about once in a minute.
此外，无论她想把槌球送到哪里，总有一条沟壑或隆起的土丘挡着；而且，倒立着的士兵们总是站起来，走到场地的其他地方，爱丽丝很快就得出结论，这真是一个非常困难的游戏。
Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, “and then,” thought she, “what would become of me?
爱丽丝开始感到很不安：当然，她还没有和王后发生争执，但知道随时可能发生，她想：“那我该怎么办？”
They’re dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there’s any one left alive!”
他们在这里非常喜欢斩首，最大的奇迹是，还有人活着！”

She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself “It’s the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to.”
她四处张望寻找逃脱的方法，又在想自己是否能不被人发现就溜走，这时她注意到空中出现了一个奇怪的景象：起初她很困惑，但看了一会儿后，她认出那是一张咧嘴笑的脸，于是她自言自语道：“是猫先生：现在我总算有人可以交谈了。”
“How are you getting on?” said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.
“你怎么样了？”猫说，它刚能开口说话。
Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded.
爱丽丝等眼睛出现后，才点了点头。
“It’s no use speaking to it,” she thought, “till its ears have come, or at least one of them.”
“还没看见耳朵呢，”她想，“说话之前，它至少要露出一只耳朵。”
In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had someone to listen to her.
又过了一分钟，猫的整个头部都出现了，于是爱丽丝放下她的火鸡，开始讲述自己的比赛，感到很高兴有人可以听她讲述。
The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.
猫似乎觉得现在它已经露出了足够的部分，于是不再让它露出更多的部分。

“I don’t think they play at all fairly,” Alice began, in rather a complaining tone, “and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can’t hear oneself speak—and they don’t seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them—and you’ve no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there’s the arch I’ve got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground—and I should have croqueted the Queen’s hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!”
“我觉得他们玩得并不公平，”爱丽丝开始抱怨道，“而且他们全都争执得非常厉害，几乎听不见自己说话了——他们似乎并没有什么特别的规则；至少，如果有什么规则的话，没有人遵守它们——你根本无法想象那混乱的场面，比如我接下来要经过的那道拱门，它就在地面的另一端，而我本可以打那只王后的小刺猬，只是它看到我的火鸡时就逃走了！”
“How do you like the Queen?” said the Cat in a low voice.
“你对王后怎么样？”猫低声说。

“Not at all,” said Alice: “she’s so extremely—” Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on, “—likely to win, that it’s hardly worth while finishing the game.”
“一点也不怎么样，”爱丽丝说，“她赢的可能性非常大，所以根本不必结束比赛了。”
The Queen smiled and passed on.
王后笑了笑，继续前行。
“Who are you talking to?” said the King, going up to Alice, and looking at the Cat’s head with great curiosity.
“你在跟谁说话？”国王说，他走近爱丽丝，用极大的好奇看着猫的头部。
“It’s a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat,” said Alice: “allow me to introduce it.”
“它是我一个朋友——一只猫先生，”爱丽丝说，“请允许我介绍它。”
“I don’t like the look of it at all,” said the King: “however, it may kiss my hand if it likes.”
“我一点也不喜欢它，”国王说，“不过它要是愿意，可以亲吻我的手。”
“I’d rather not,” the Cat remarked.
“我不愿意，”猫说。
“Don’t be impertinent,” said the King, “and don’t look at me like that!”
“不要无礼，”国王说，“不要看我那样！”
He got behind Alice as he spoke.
他说话时就站在爱丽丝身后。
“A cat may look at a king,” said Alice.
“猫儿可以瞧瞧国王，”爱丽丝说。
“I’ve read that in some book, but I don’t remember where.”
“我在一本书上读到过这句话，不过我记不得是在哪本书上读到的了。”
“Well, it must be removed,” said the King very decidedly, and he called the Queen, who was passing at the moment, “My dear!
“嗯，那必须得移走了，”国王非常果断地说，并且他正巧经过，就叫了正在经过的王后，“亲爱的！
I wish you would have this cat removed!”
我希望你能把这只猫移走！”
The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small.
无论大小问题，女王解决起来都只有一个办法。
“Off with his head!” she said, without even looking round.
“砍了它的头！”她毫不迟疑地说，连头都没回。
“I’ll fetch the executioner myself,” said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.
“我自己去叫刽子手来，”国王急切地说，然后就匆匆地走了。
Alice thought she might as well go back, and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen’s voice in the distance, screaming with passion.
爱丽丝心想，她倒不如回去看看，游戏进行得怎么样了，因为她听到女王的声音在远处，正大喊大叫。

She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not.
她已经听到三个玩家被判处斩首，因为他们错过了他们的回合，她对游戏的局势并不看好，因为游戏混乱得她根本不知道该不该轮到她。
So she went in search of her hedgehog.
所以她去找她的刺猬。

The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.
刺猬正在和另一只刺猬打斗，对于爱丽丝来说，这是一个绝佳的机会，可以利用另一只刺猬来击打其中一只：唯一的困难是，她的火鸡已经飞到花园的另一边去了，爱丽丝可以看到它无助地试图飞到树上。

By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight: “but it doesn’t matter much,” thought Alice, “as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground.”
等她抓到火鸡并把它带回时，战斗已经结束了，两只刺猬都看不见了：“不过没关系，”爱丽丝心想，“因为所有的拱门都从这边消失了。”
So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back for a little more conversation with her friend.
所以她把火鸡夹在腋下，以防它再次逃跑，然后回去和她的朋友继续谈话。

When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.
当她回到猫头鹰那里时，她惊讶地发现那里聚集了一大群人：刽子手、国王和王后正在争论，其他人则在安静地争论，而其他人看起来很不舒服。

The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard indeed to make out exactly what they said.
爱丽丝一出现，三人都要求她裁决，还把各自的论点重复了一遍，虽然他们同时说话，她实在很难分辨他们到底在说什么。

The executioner’s argument was, that you couldn’t cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn’t going to begin at his time of life.
执行官的论点是，除非有身体，否则不能砍掉脑袋，他以前从未遇到过这种情况，也不会在自己这个年纪开始。
The King’s argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren’t to talk nonsense.
国王的论点是，任何有脑袋的东西都可以砍掉脑袋，不能胡言乱语。
The Queen’s argument was, that if something wasn’t done about it in less than no time she’d have everybody executed, all round.
皇后说，如果不到一分钟内不采取行动，她就要把所有人处决。
(It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)
（正是这个最后一句话，让整个宴会显得如此严肃紧张。）
Alice could think of nothing else to say but “It belongs to the Duchess: you’d better ask her about it.”
爱丽丝能想出来的唯一一句话就是“它属于那位女爵，你最好去问她”。
“She’s in prison,” the Queen said to the executioner: “fetch her here.”
“她在监狱里，”皇后对执行官说，“把她叫来。”
And the executioner went off like an arrow.
执行官像箭一样地走了出去。

The Cat’s head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.
执行官一走，猫头就逐渐消失，等他带着女爵回来时，猫头已经完全消失不见了，所以国王和执行官疯狂地跑来跑去寻找猫头，而宴会的其他人都回到游戏里去了。

ch.et: Chapter IX. The Mock Turtle’s Story
ch.zt: 第九章 · 假海龟的故事
p: “You can’t think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!” said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice’s, and they walked off together.
“你再见到我真是太高兴了，你这老朋友！”鸭子太太说，她亲昵地把胳膊挽进爱丽丝的臂弯里，两人一起走开了。
Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
Alice 觉得 很 高興 在 厨房 跟 她 相遇 時 她 的 氣質 很 悶 ； 自言 自語 道 可能 是 胡椒 做 的 她 那 時 很 暴躁 。
“When I’m a Duchess,” she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though), “I won’t have any pepper in my kitchen at all.
“当我是公爵夫人的时候，”她自言自语道，（不过语气并不很乐观），“我的厨房里就不会再放胡椒了。

Soup does very well without—Maybe it’s always pepper that makes people hot-tempered,” she went on, very much pleased at having found out a new kind of rule, “and vinegar that makes them sour—and camomile that makes them bitter—and—and barley-sugar and such things that make children sweet-tempered.
汤里没有胡椒也很好——也许总是胡椒使人生气，醋使人生闷气，甘菊使人生气，糖果使人生气——糖果和类似的东西使人生气——孩子们则生甜气。
I only wish people knew that: then they wouldn’t be so stingy about it, you know—”
只有我希望人们知道：那样的话，他们就不会那么吝啬了，你知道的——“
She had quite forgotten the Duchess by this time, and was a little startled when she heard her voice close to her ear.
她这时已经把温格夫人忘得一干二净，听到她近在耳畔的声音，不禁吃了一惊。
“You’re thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk.
你正想着什么，我的 dear ，那让你忘了说话。
I can’t tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit.”
我不能现在告诉你那是什么意思，但我会记住的。
“Perhaps it hasn’t one,” Alice ventured to remark.
“或许它没有一个，”爱丽丝试探着说道。
“Tut, tut, child!” said the Duchess.
“嘘，孩子，” Duchess 哼道。
“Everything’s got a moral, if only you can find it.”
一切都有其教训，只是你可能找不到。
And she squeezed herself up closer to Alice’s side as she spoke.
她挤得更靠近爱丽丝身边说话。

Alice did not much like keeping so close to her: first, because the Duchess was very ugly; and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice’s shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin.
爱丽丝并不太喜欢紧挨着她：首先，因为王后非常难看；其次，她的身高正好可以搁在爱丽丝肩上，而且这下巴尖得有点不舒服。
However, she did not like to be rude, so she bore it as well as she could.
然而，她不喜欢给人不礼貌的感觉，所以她尽量忍受。
“The game’s going on rather better now,” she said, by way of keeping up the conversation a little.
“游戏现在进行得不错了，”她说道，聊以慰情。
“’Tis so,” said the Duchess: “and the moral of that is—‘Oh, ’tis love, ’tis love, that makes the world go round!’”
“是啊，”厨娘说：“那故事的教训是——‘哦，是爱情，是爱情，让世界运转起来啊！’”
“Somebody said,” Alice whispered, “that it’s done by everybody minding their own business!”
“有人说过，”爱丽丝小声说，“是每个人都管好自己的事！”
“Ah, well!
啊，好吧！

It means much the same thing,” said the Duchess, digging her sharp little chin into Alice’s shoulder as she added, “and the moral of that is—‘Take care of the sense, and the sounds will take care of themselves.’”
它意思大同小异，”鸭子说道，用她尖尖的小下巴抵了抵爱丽丝的肩膀，接着又说：“那故事的教训是——‘好好照顾了逻辑，剩下的自然就会照顾好了。’”
“How fond she is of finding morals in things!”
多么喜欢从事物中发现道理啊！
Alice thought to herself.
爱丽丝自言自语。
“I dare say you’re wondering why I don’t put my arm round your waist,” the Duchess said after a pause: “the reason is, that I’m doubtful about the temper of your flamingo.
“我想你一定在奇怪，我为什么没有把你搂在怀里，”那女人大声说，停顿了一下，“因为，我怀疑你那红鸟的脾气。”
Shall I try the experiment?”
试试这个实验吗？
“He might bite,” Alice cautiously replied, not feeling at all anxious to have the experiment tried.
他可能会咬的，”爱丽丝谨慎地回答，一点也不觉得尝试这个实验有什么不妥。
“Very true,” said the Duchess: “flamingoes and mustard both bite.
“非常对，”那女巫说：“ flamingoes和mustard都咬。”
And the moral of that is—‘Birds of a feather flock together.’”
和这则寓言的道理是一样的——“物以类聚，人以群分”。
“Only mustard isn’t a bird,” Alice remarked.
只有芥末不是一只鸟，爱丽丝 remark。
“Right, as usual,” said the Duchess: “what a clear way you have of putting things!”
“It’s a mineral, I think,” said Alice.
它是矿物质，我想。
“Of course it is,” said the Duchess, who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said; “there’s a large mustard-mine near here.
“当然有，”那女人大声说，她似乎对爱丽丝说的每一句话都表示赞同；“这里附近有一个大芥末矿。”
And the moral of that is—‘The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours.’”
And the moral of that is—“拥有越多，你的就越少。”
“Oh, I know!” exclaimed Alice, who had not attended to this last remark, “it’s a vegetable.
“哦，我知道了！”爱丽丝喊道，她没注意到最后那句话，“是蔬菜。”
It doesn’t look like one, but it is.”
它看起来不像一个，但它是。

“I quite agree with you,” said the Duchess; “and the moral of that is—‘Be what you would seem to be’—or if you’d like it put more simply—‘Never imagine yourself not to be otherwise than what it might appear to others that what you were or might have been was not otherwise than what you had been would have appeared to them to be otherwise.’”
“我完全同意你的说法，”那女巫说，“那故事的教训是——‘要成为你看起来像的人’——或者如果用更简单的说法——‘不要想象自己不是别人所想象的你不是的样子，你本来的样子如果别人想象你本来的样子不是，那样子就不是你本来的样子。’”
“I think I should understand that better,” Alice said very politely, “if I had it written down: but I can’t quite follow it as you say it.”
我心想如果能写下来我也许会懂一些，”爱丽丝很客气地说，“可是你这么说我还是不太明白。
“That’s nothing to what I could say if I chose,” the Duchess replied, in a pleased tone.
那比起我说的还差远了，如果我愿意说的话。 Duchess 笑着回答。
“Pray don’t trouble yourself to say it any longer than that,” said Alice.
请不要再说下去了，”爱丽丝说。
“Oh, don’t talk about trouble!” said the Duchess.
“哦，不要提麻烦的事儿！” Duchess 说。
“I make you a present of everything I’ve said as yet.”
“我送你刚才所说的一切。”
“A cheap sort of present!” thought Alice.
“便宜的东西！”爱丽丝想道。
“I’m glad they don’t give birthday presents like that!”
我很高兴他们不会送那样的生日礼物！
But she did not venture to say it out loud.
但她没有胆量把它说出来。
“Thinking again?” the Duchess asked, with another dig of her sharp little chin.
“又在想什么？”王后又用她尖尖的小下巴嘲讽地问。
“I’ve a right to think,” said Alice sharply, for she was beginning to feel a little worried.
“我有权利思考，”爱丽丝尖锐地说，因为她开始有点担心了。
“Just about as much right,” said the Duchess, “as pigs have to fly; and the m—”
“差不多一样正确，”厨娘说，“猪飞得和马一样高；和马——”
But here, to Alice’s great surprise, the Duchess’s voice died away, even in the middle of her favourite word ‘moral,’ and the arm that was linked into hers began to tremble.
但是在这里，令爱丽丝大吃一惊的是，王后的声音渐渐低了下去，即使在她最喜欢的词“道德”中间，那只和她相握的手也开始颤抖了。
Alice looked up, and there stood the Queen in front of them, with her arms folded, frowning like a thunderstorm.
Alice抬头，只见王后站在他们面前，双手交叉，眉头紧锁，像要发怒似的。
“A fine day, your Majesty!” the Duchess began in a low, weak voice.
“陛下，好天气啊！”那女巫用低而微弱的声音说道。
“Now, I give you fair warning,” shouted the Queen, stamping on the ground as she spoke; “either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time!
“现在，我警告你了，”王后说着跺了跺脚，“要么你要么你的脑袋，得在大约半小时内被摘下来！”
Take your choice!”
你选吧！
The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.
Duchess选了一样，立刻就走了。
“Let’s go on with the game,” the Queen said to Alice; and Alice was too much frightened to say a word, but slowly followed her back to the croquet-ground.

The other guests had taken advantage of the Queen’s absence, and were resting in the shade: however, the moment they saw her, they hurried back to the game, the Queen merely remarking that a moment’s delay would cost them their lives.
其他客人趁着王后不在，已经在树荫下休息；然而，一看到她，他们立刻又回到游戏中去，王后只是说耽搁片刻就要他们的命了。
All the time they were playing the Queen never left off quarrelling with the other players, and shouting “Off with his head!” or “Off with her head!”
他们玩的时候，王后从来没有停止过跟其他玩家争吵，喊着“砍掉他的头！”或者“砍掉她的头！”

Those whom she sentenced were taken into custody by the soldiers, who of course had to leave off being arches to do this, so that by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left, and all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody and under sentence of execution.
那些她判处的人，被士兵带走，当然，士兵们不得不放下拱形的姿势去做这件事，所以不到半个小时，就没有拱形了，所有的玩家，除了国王、皇后和爱丽丝，都被关押，面临死刑。
Then the Queen left off, quite out of breath, and said to Alice, “Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?”
然后，那皇后喘着气，说：“你见过那嘲弄的龟了吗？”
“No,” said Alice.
“不，”爱丽丝说。
“I don’t even know what a Mock Turtle is.”
我也不知道mock turtle是什么。
“It’s the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from,” said the Queen.
它是 MOCK TURTLE 浇头汤的原料，女王说。
“I never saw one, or heard of one,” said Alice.
我从来没有见过，也没有听说过。
“Come on, then,” said the Queen, “and he shall tell you his history.”
“走吧，”王后说，“他可以给你讲他的故事。”
As they walked off together, Alice heard the King say in a low voice, to the company generally, “You are all pardoned.”
作为他们一起走开时，爱丽丝听到国王小声对大家说：“你们都被赦免了。”
“Come, that’s a good thing!” she said to herself, for she had felt quite unhappy at the number of executions the Queen had ordered.
“来，那是个好东西！”她对自己说，因为女王下令处死的人数太多，她感到很不开心。
They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun.
他们很快就遇到了一只睡在阳光下的 Gryphon 。
(If you don’t know what a Gryphon is, look at the picture.)
如果你不知道 Gryphon 是什么，看看插图。
“Up, lazy thing!” said the Queen, “and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history.
“上，懒虫！”王后说，“带这位年轻 lady 去见 Mock Turtle，听听他的故事。”
I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered;” and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon.
我必须回去看看我下令执行的一些死刑；”说完，她便走了，只留下 Alice 一个人和 Gryphon。
Alice did not quite like the look of the creature, but on the whole she thought it would be quite as safe to stay with it as to go after that savage Queen: so she waited.
Alice 对那只生物的长相并不太满意，不过总体上她觉得与其跟着那只野蛮女王，还不如跟着它安全，所以她就等着了。
The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes: then it watched the Queen till she was out of sight: then it chuckled.
狮鹫坐起来揉揉眼睛，然后一直盯着女王看，直到女王消失不见，狮鹫才发出咯咯的笑声。
“What fun!” said the Gryphon, half to itself, half to Alice.
“多好玩啊！”那只龙半自言自语，半对爱丽丝说。
“What is the fun?” said Alice.
“有什么好玩的？”爱丽丝说。
“Why, she,” said the Gryphon.
“咦，” Gryphon 说。
“It’s all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know.
她们从不真的杀任何人，你知道。
Come on!”
快点！
“Everybody says ‘come on!’ here,” thought Alice, as she went slowly after it: “I never was so ordered about in all my life, never!”
everybody都说“快点！”这里，”爱丽丝心想，她慢慢地跟随着它走：“我这一生从来没有被这么指挥过，从来没有!”

They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break.
他们往前走了没多久，就看见远处有一个“考姆特鲁”坐在一块小岩石上，神情悲伤孤独，走近一看，爱丽丝听见他叹气，仿佛心都要碎了。
She pitied him deeply.
她对他深感同情。
“What is his sorrow?” she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, very nearly in the same words as before, “It’s all his fancy, that: he hasn’t got no sorrow, you know.
他有什么烦恼？”，她问 Gryphon，Gryphon 也几乎用同样的话回答：“那全是他的幻想，他没有烦恼，你知道。”
Come on!”
快 come on!
So they went up to the Mock Turtle, who looked at them with large eyes full of tears, but said nothing.
于是他们走到 Mock Turtle 那里， Mock Turtle 用大眼睛含着泪看着他们，但什么也没说。
“This here young lady,” said the Gryphon, “she wants for to know your history, she do.”
“这个年轻的女士，” Gryphon 说，“她想知道你的故事，她是这样想的。”
“I’ll tell it her,” said the Mock Turtle in a deep, hollow tone: “sit down, both of you, and don’t speak a word till I’ve finished.”
我告诉她， Mock Turtle 说， 且慢说话， 让我讲完了你们再坐下。
So they sat down, and nobody spoke for some minutes.
于是他们坐下，过了好一会儿谁也没有说话。
Alice thought to herself, “I don’t see how he can ever finish, if he doesn’t begin.”
Alice 自言自语道：“我看他怎么也完成不了，除非他先开始。”
But she waited patiently.
但是她耐心地等待着。
“Once,” said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, “I was a real Turtle.”
“Once,” said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, “我是一只真正的 turtle。”
These words were followed by a very long silence, broken only by an occasional exclamation of “Hjckrrh!” from the Gryphon, and the constant heavy sobbing of the Mock Turtle.
这些话后跟着一个非常长久的沉默，偶尔传来一声“呼呼！”的 Gryphon 喘息声，以及 Mock Turtle 持续沉重的抽泣声。
Alice was very nearly getting up and saying, “Thank you, sir, for your interesting story,” but she could not help thinking there must be more to come, so she sat still and said nothing.
Alice 走了幾步，準備說聲“謝謝，先生，您有趣的故事”，但她不能不想到故事還會有下文，所以她坐著不說話。
“When we were little,” the Mock Turtle went on at last, more calmly, though still sobbing a little now and then, “we went to school in the sea.
“当我们还是小家伙的时候，” Mock Turtle最后冷静地继续说道，尽管时不时地还抽噎着，“我们在海里上学。”
The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise—”
The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise”—“上一句（仅供参考，不要翻译）
“Why did you call him Tortoise, if he wasn’t one?”
“为什么你叫他乌龟，如果他不是乌龟呢？”
Alice asked.
爱丽丝问道。
“We called him Tortoise because he taught us,” said the Mock Turtle angrily: “really you are very dull!”
我们叫他乌龟，因为他教过我们，” MOCK TURTLE 愤怒地说，“你真是太笨了！”
“You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question,” added the Gryphon; and then they both sat silent and looked at poor Alice, who felt ready to sink into the earth.
“你问这么简单的问题，应该感到羞愧，” Gryphon 说道，然后他们俩都沉默了，看着可怜的爱丽丝，她觉得自己快要被大地吞没。
At last the Gryphon said to the Mock Turtle, “Drive on, old fellow!
最后 Gryphon 对 Mock Turtle 说：“继续说，老兄！”
Don’t be all day about it!” and he went on in these words:
别磨蹭了！他接着说：
“Yes, we went to school in the sea, though you mayn’t believe it—”
“是的，我们去海里的学校了，不过你可能不信——”
“I never said I didn’t!” interrupted Alice.
“我可没说我不行！”爱丽丝打断道。
“You did,” said the Mock Turtle.
“你确实做到了，” Mock Turtle 说。
“Hold your tongue!” added the Gryphon, before Alice could speak again.
别说话！那只龙狮提醒了爱丽丝，她还没来得及开口。
The Mock Turtle went on.
Mock Turtle继续说道。
“We had the best of educations—in fact, we went to school every day—”
“我们接受最好的教育——事实上，我们每天都去上学——”
“I’ve been to a day-school, too,” said Alice; “you needn’t be so proud as all that.”
“我也上过一天学校，”爱丽丝说，“你也不用这么自夸。”
“With extras?” asked the Mock Turtle a little anxiously.
“With extras?”问 Mock Turtle 稍微有些焦急。
“Yes,” said Alice, “we learned French and music.”
“是的，”爱丽丝说，“我们学了法语和音乐。”
“And washing?” said the Mock Turtle.
“Certainly not!” said Alice indignantly.
当然不！” Alice indignantly said。
“Ah! then yours wasn’t a really good school,” said the Mock Turtle in a tone of great relief.
啊！那么你的学校并不是一所好学校，” Mock Turtle 说，听起来非常庆幸。
“Now at ours they had at the end of the bill, ‘French, music, and washing—extra.’”
“他们账单的末尾写着：‘法式服务，音乐，洗衣，额外收费。’”
“You couldn’t have wanted it much,” said Alice; “living at the bottom of the sea.”
“你不可能想要得这么强烈，”爱丽丝说，“住在海底底部。”
“I couldn’t afford to learn it.” said the Mock Turtle with a sigh.
“我付不起学费。” Mock Turtle 说，叹了口气。
“I only took the regular course.”
“我只是按照正常课程走的。”
“What was that?” inquired Alice.
“那是什么？”爱丽丝问道。
“Reeling and Writhing, of course, to begin with,” the Mock Turtle replied; “and then the different branches of Arithmetic—Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision.”
上身摇摇晃晃，先是这样开始， Mock Turtle回答说； “然后是算术的不同门类——野心、分心、丑化和嘲笑。”
“I never heard of ‘Uglification,’” Alice ventured to say.
“我从没听说过‘丑化’这个词，”爱丽丝试探着说。
“What is it?”
“这是什么？”
The Gryphon lifted up both its paws in surprise.
狮鹫同时抬起两只前爪惊讶地。
“What!
Never heard of uglifying!” it exclaimed.
“从未听说过丑化！”它 exclaimed。
“You know what to beautify is, I suppose?”
“你该知道美化是什么吧？”
“Yes,” said Alice doubtfully: “it means—to—make—anything—prettier.”
“是的，”爱丽丝有点犹豫地说：“意思是——使任何东西——更漂亮。”
“Well, then,” the Gryphon went on, “if you don’t know what to uglify is, you are a simpleton.”
“Well, then,” the Gryphon went on, “如果你不知道该如何丑化是什么，你就是一个傻子。”
Alice did not feel encouraged to ask any more questions about it, so she turned to the Mock Turtle, and said “What else had you to learn?”
爱丽丝没有感到有问更多问题的鼓励，于是她转向 MOCK 老 Turtle，问道：“你还学了什么？”

“Well, there was Mystery,” the Mock Turtle replied, counting off the subjects on his flappers, “—Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography: then Drawling—the Drawling-master was an old conger-eel, that used to come once a week: he taught us Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils.”
“嗯，有谜语，” MOCK TURTLE 回答，数着自己的翅膀：“——古代的谜语和现代的谜语，还有航海学：然后是绘画——绘画老师是一条老鳕鱼，每周来一次：他教我们绘画、伸展和晕厥。”
“What was that like?” said Alice.
那是什么？爱丽丝问。
“Well, I can’t show it you myself,” the Mock Turtle said: “I’m too stiff.
Well, 我自己是不能让你看的，” Mock Turtle 说：“我太僵硬了。
And the Gryphon never learnt it.”
那只龙猫从未学会。
“Hadn’t time,” said the Gryphon: “I went to the Classics master, though.
“没时间，” Gryphon 说：“我去过古典文学老师那了。”
He was an old crab, he was.”
他是个老蟹，“。
“I never went to him,” the Mock Turtle said with a sigh: “he taught Laughing and Grief, they used to say.”
我从不曾去他那里， Mock Turtle 说，带着一声长叹 ： “他们说他教过欢笑和悲哀。”
“So he did, so he did,” said the Gryphon, sighing in his turn; and both creatures hid their faces in their paws.
“他确实如此，他确实如此，”龙公叹息着说，两只生物把脸埋在爪子中间。
“And how many hours a day did you do lessons?” said Alice, in a hurry to change the subject.
“你一天要上多少个小时的课啊？”爱丽丝连忙改变话题说。
“Ten hours the first day,” said the Mock Turtle: “nine the next, and so on.”
“第一天十小时，第二天九小时，” Mock Turtle said：“以后依次类推。”
“What a curious plan!” exclaimed Alice.
“奇哉妙哉一个计划！”爱丽丝惊呼。
“That’s the reason they’re called lessons,” the Gryphon remarked: “because they lessen from day to day.”
那是因为叫功课，”龙说：“因为每天都在减少。
This was quite a new idea to Alice, and she thought it over a little before she made her next remark.
这在爱丽丝看来还是一个新想法，她先仔细想了想，才又说下去。
“Then the eleventh day must have been a holiday?”
“那么第十一天一定是假日了？”
“Of course it was,” said the Mock Turtle.
当然了，” Mock Turtle said。
“And how did you manage on the twelfth?”
“你十二点是怎么过去的？”
Alice went on eagerly.
爱丽丝急急忙忙地继续往前走。
“That’s enough about lessons,” the Gryphon interrupted in a very decided tone: “tell her something about the games now.”
“那够了，关于功课的事，” Gryphon 以坚定的语气打断了 Alice：“现在告诉她一些游戏的事。”

ch.zt: 第十章 · 龙虾方块舞
p: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes.
莫克龟深深叹了口气，用一只翅膀的背面抹了抹眼睛。
He looked at Alice, and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice.
他看着爱丽丝，试图说话，但一会儿工夫，他的声音被呜咽声哽住了。
“Same as if he had a bone in his throat,” said the Gryphon: and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back.
“就像喉咙里有一根骨头似的。”那只独角兽说，它开始摇晃他、捶打他的背部。
At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again:—
最后，莫克龟恢复了声音，眼泪顺着脸颊流下来，他继续说：

“You may not have lived much under the sea—” (“I haven’t,” said Alice)—“and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster—” (Alice began to say “I once tasted—” but checked herself hastily, and said “No, never”) “—so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster Quadrille is!”
“你可能没在海里生活过——”（“我没有”爱丽丝说）“而且你也许从未被介绍过龙虾——”（爱丽丝想说“我曾经品尝过”但急忙打断自己，说“没有”）“——所以你一定不知道龙虾四重奏是多么美妙！”
“No, indeed,” said Alice.
“没有，”爱丽丝说。
“What sort of a dance is it?”
“是什么样的舞蹈？”
“Why,” said the Gryphon, “you first form into a line along the sea-shore—”
“嗯，”独角兽说，“你首先沿着海岸排成一行——”
“Two lines!” cried the Mock Turtle.
“两行！”莫克龟喊道。
“Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on; then, when you’ve cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—”
“海豹、海龟、鲑鱼等等；然后，当你把所有的海蜇清理掉——”
“That generally takes some time,” interrupted the Gryphon.
“那通常需要一些时间，”独角兽打断了莫克龟。
“—you advance twice—”
“——你前进两次——”
“Each with a lobster as a partner!” cried the Gryphon.
“每次都有一位龙虾作为搭档！”独角兽喊道。
“Of course,” the Mock Turtle said: “advance twice, set to partners—”
“当然，”莫克龟说：“前进两次，配对——”
“—change lobsters, and retire in same order,” continued the Gryphon.
“——交换龙虾，然后按原顺序后退，”独角兽继续说。
“Then, you know,” the Mock Turtle went on, “you throw the—”
“然后你知道，” Mock Turtle继续说，“你抛的——”
“The lobsters!” shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.
“螃蟹们！” Gryphon 一声尖叫，纵身跃入空中。
“—as far out to sea as you can—”
“像离海有多远你就游到多远——”
“Swim after them!” screamed the Gryphon.
冲向他们游去！ Gryphon大叫。
“Turn a somersault in the sea!” cried the Mock Turtle, capering wildly about.
转身在海里做一个回旋踢！ Mock Turtle wildly about 喊着，旋转跳跃。
“Change lobsters again!” yelled the Gryphon at the top of its voice.
“变变变！变变变！” Gryphon 在尖叫声中大喊。

“Back to land again, and that’s all the first figure,” said the Mock Turtle, suddenly dropping his voice; and the two creatures, who had been jumping about like mad things all this time, sat down again very sadly and quietly, and looked at Alice.
“回到陆地上去，那就是第一幅图了，” Mock Turtle 突然压低了声音说道；而那两只一直跳来跳去像发了疯似的所有东西，现在也坐下来非常悲伤地、安静地，看着 Alice。
“It must be a very pretty dance,” said Alice timidly.
“一定是很美丽的舞蹈吧，”爱丽丝小心翼翼地说。
“Would you like to see a little of it?” said the Mock Turtle.
“你要不要看看一点点？” MOCK TURTLE 问。
“Very much indeed,” said Alice.
“非常地，”爱丽丝说。
“Come, let’s try the first figure!” said the Mock Turtle to the Gryphon.
“来吧，我们先试第一个图形！” Mock Turtle对 Gryphon 说。
“We can do without lobsters, you know.
我们可以不用虾蟹，你知道的。
Which shall sing?”
哪一首歌我们来唱？
“Oh, you sing,” said the Gryphon.
“哦，你会唱歌呢，” Gryphon 说。
“I’ve forgotten the words.”
“我忘了歌词了。”

So they began solemnly dancing round and round Alice, every now and then treading on her toes when they passed too close, and waving their forepaws to mark the time, while the Mock Turtle sang this, very slowly and sadly:—
So他们开始庄严地围着Alice跳舞，每过一会儿就踩到她的脚尖上，当他们靠近时，而嘲讽的乌龟唱着这首歌，非常缓慢而悲伤地：—
“Will you walk a little faster?” said a whiting to a snail.
“你走快一点好吗？”一只鰭魚對蜗牛說。
“There’s a porpoise close behind us, and he’s treading on my tail.
有一个海豚紧贴着我们，他踩着我的尾巴。
See how eagerly the lobsters and the turtles all advance!
看那龙虾和乌龟都急急忙忙地向前挤！
They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance?
他们正在卵石上等着——你来加入跳舞吗？
Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance?
你来不来，你来不来，你来不来，你来不来，你来不来 join the dance?
Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, won’t you join the dance?
你会不会，不会你会不会不会你会不会 join 这个舞？
“You can really have no notion how delightful it will be When they take us up and throw us, with the lobsters, out to sea!”
“你根本无法想象他们会把我们抱起来，然后像螃蟹一样扔到海里去！”
But the snail replied “Too far, too far!” and gave a look askance— Said he thanked the whiting kindly, but he would not join the dance.
但蜗牛回答：“太远了，太远了！”并斜睨一眼—— 他说感谢了蛤蜊，但不会加入舞会。
Would not, could not, would not, could not, would not join the dance.
不愿，不能，不愿加入舞蹈。
Would not, could not, would not, could not, could not join the dance.
不愿意，不能，不愿意，不能，不能加入舞蹈。
“What matters it how far we go?” his scaly friend replied.
“走到哪里都无所谓，”他的鳞片朋友回答。
“There is another shore, you know, upon the other side.
那里还有另一岸，你知道，在另一边。
The further off from England the nearer is to France— Then turn not pale, beloved snail, but come and join the dance.
更远的英格兰就是更接近法国了——那么不要害怕，亲爱的蜗牛，快 join the dance 来吧。
Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance?
你会不会，不会你会，不会你会，加入舞蹈？
Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, won’t you join the dance?”
“你要不要，要不要，要不要，要不要，要不要加入舞蹈？”
“Thank you, it’s a very interesting dance to watch,” said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last: “and I do so like that curious song about the whiting!”
“谢谢，看这个有趣的舞蹈真是太有趣了，最后终于结束了：‘而且我非常喜欢关于白鱼的那首奇怪的歌！’”
“Oh, as to the whiting,” said the Mock Turtle, “they—you’ve seen them, of course?”
“哦，至于白鱼，” Mock Turtle 说，“你当然见过它们，对吧？”
“Yes,” said Alice, “I’ve often seen them at dinn—” she checked herself hastily.
“是的，” Alice 回答，“我经常在餐——”她急忙中断了自己。
“I don’t know where Dinn may be,” said the Mock Turtle, “but if you’ve seen them so often, of course you know what they’re like.”
我不晓得晚餐在哪里，” Mock Turtle说，“不过既然你这么常看见他们，当然也知道他们是什么样子了。
“I believe so,” Alice replied thoughtfully.
“我相信是这样，” Alice 说，她想了一下。
“They have their tails in their mouths—and they’re all over crumbs.”
“它们把尾巴都咬在嘴里——它们都是满嘴面包屑。”
“You’re wrong about the crumbs,” said the Mock Turtle: “crumbs would all wash off in the sea.
你关于 crumbs 的说法是错的，” Mock Turtle 说：“在海里洗一洗， crumbs 都会洗掉。
But they have their tails in their mouths; and the reason is—” here the Mock Turtle yawned and shut his eyes.—“Tell her about the reason and all that,” he said to the Gryphon.
但他们的尾巴在嘴里；原因是因为—”说到这里， MOCK 龟打了个哈欠，合上眼睛。“告诉她原因和一切，”他对龙说。
“The reason is,” said the Gryphon, “that they would go with the lobsters to the dance.
“原因就是，” Gryphon 说，“它们会跟螃蟹一起去跳舞。
So they got thrown out to sea.
所以它们被扔到海里。
So they had to fall a long way.
所以它们得往下掉很长一段路。
So they got their tails fast in their mouths.
所以它们的尾巴卡在嘴里。
So they couldn’t get them out again.
所以它们再也取不出来了。
That’s all.”
就是这样。”
“Thank you,” said Alice, “it’s very interesting.
谢谢你，爱丽丝说，“这很有趣。”
I never knew so much about a whiting before.”
我从前从没听说过什么whiting。
“I can tell you more than that, if you like,” said the Gryphon.
我可以告诉你更多，如果你愿意。
“Do you know why it’s called a whiting?”
“你知道为什么叫作‘白鲸’吗？”
“I never thought about it,” said Alice.
我从来没有想过这一点，爱丽丝说。
“Why?”
“为什么？”
“It does the boots and shoes,” the Gryphon replied very solemnly.
“它替靴子和鞋定型，”龙鸟严肃地说。
Alice was thoroughly puzzled.
爱丽丝感到十分困惑。
“Does the boots and shoes!” she repeated in a wondering tone.
“穿靴子还是穿鞋呢？”她迷惑地重复着。
“Why, what are your shoes done with?” said the Gryphon.
“咦，你的靴子是什么做的？” Gryphon 说道。
“I mean, what makes them so shiny?”
“我指的是，它们为什么这么亮？”
Alice looked down at them, and considered a little before she gave her answer.
Alice低头看着他们，略加考虑后才回答。
“They’re done with blacking, I believe.”
它们已经完成黑魔法了，我想。
“Boots and shoes under the sea,” the Gryphon went on in a deep voice, “are done with a whiting.
“海里的靴子和鞋子，”龙虾继续用低沉的声音说道，“是用白虾做的。”
Now you know.”
你现在知道啦。
“And what are they made of?”
它们是由什么做成的？
Alice asked in a tone of great curiosity.
Alice好奇地问道。
“Soles and eels, of course,” the Gryphon replied rather impatiently: “any shrimp could have told you that.”
虾和鳗鱼，当然了，”龙公爵不耐烦地答道：“任何一个虾都可以告诉你。”
“If I’d been the whiting,” said Alice, whose thoughts were still running on the song, “I’d have said to the porpoise, ‘Keep back, please: we don’t want you with us!’”
“如果我是白颊鱼，”爱丽丝说，她还在想着那首歌，“我会对海豚说：‘请退后，我们不要你跟我们在一起！’”
“They were obliged to have him with them,” the Mock Turtle said: “no wise fish would go anywhere without a porpoise.”
它们不得不带他一起，” Mock Turtle说：“没有一条聪明的鱼会去任何地方不带一个海豚。
“Wouldn’t it really?” said Alice in a tone of great surprise.
“真的会是这样吗？”爱丽丝惊讶地说道。
“Of course not,” said the Mock Turtle: “why, if a fish came to me, and told me he was going a journey, I should say ‘With what porpoise?’”
当然不，” Mock Turtle said：“如果一条鱼告诉我它要去旅行，我会说‘用什么目的？’’”
“Don’t you mean ‘purpose’?” said Alice.
“你不是说‘目的’吗？”爱丽丝说。
“I mean what I say,” the Mock Turtle replied in an offended tone.
我所说的是我所说的， Mock Turtle 以一种受了冒犯的语气回答。
And the Gryphon added “Come, let’s hear some of your adventures.”
“I could tell you my adventures—beginning from this morning,” said Alice a little timidly: “but it’s no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.”
“我可以告诉你我的奇遇——从今天早上开始，”爱丽丝有点胆怯地说：“但是回到昨天去说已经没用了，因为我那时是个不同的我。”
“Explain all that,” said the Mock Turtle.
解释 all that, said the Mock Turtle。
“No, no!
“不，不！
The adventures first,” said the Gryphon in an impatient tone: “explanations take such a dreadful time.”
“冒险先说，” Gryphon 不耐烦地说：“解释花的时间太可怕了。”
So Alice began telling them her adventures from the time when she first saw the White Rabbit.
于是爱丽丝便开始向他们讲述她第一次见到白兔时的经历。
She was a little nervous about it just at first, the two creatures got so close to her, one on each side, and opened their eyes and mouths so very wide, but she gained courage as she went on.
她一开始对它们如此靠近感到有些紧张，一个在她的左边，一个在她的右边，眼睛和嘴巴张得如此之大，但她继续下去时，她渐渐有了勇气。

Her listeners were perfectly quiet till she got to the part about her repeating “You are old, Father William,” to the Caterpillar, and the words all coming different, and then the Mock Turtle drew a long breath, and said “That’s very curious.”
她的听众一直非常安静，直到她说到她重复“威廉先生，你老了”给毛毛虫，而且所有的词都变得不同了，这时，嘲讽海龟长长地吸了一口气，说“那真是非常奇怪。”
“It’s all about as curious as it can be,” said the Gryphon.
“那真是非常奇怪，”嘲讽海龟说。
“It all came different!” the Mock Turtle repeated thoughtfully.
“那真是非常奇怪，”嘲讽海龟又想了一遍。
“I should like to hear her try and repeat something now.
“我想听听她现在试着重复一些东西。”
Tell her to begin.”
“让她开始吧。”
He looked at the Gryphon as if he thought it had some kind of authority over Alice.
他看着嘲讽海龟，好像它对爱丽丝有某种权威似的。
“Stand up and repeat ‘’Tis the voice of the sluggard,’” said the Gryphon.
“站起来，重复‘懒惰者的嗓音’吧，”嘲讽海龟说。
“How the creatures order one about, and make one repeat lessons!” thought Alice; “I might as well be at school at once.”
“那些生物怎么命令我，怎么让我重复功课啊！”爱丽丝想道，“我还不如现在就去上学呢。”
However, she got up, and began to repeat it, but her head was so full of the Lobster Quadrille, that she hardly knew what she was saying, and the words came very queer indeed:—
然而，她站了起来，开始重复，但她脑子里满是大龙虾四重奏，以致她几乎不知道自己在说什么，而且那些词听起来很奇怪——
“’Tis the voice of the Lobster; I heard him declare, “You have baked me too brown, I must sugar my hair.”
“懒惰者的嗓音，我听到他宣称，‘你把我烤得太焦了，我得用糖来梳理我的头发。’”
As a duck with its eyelids, so he with his nose Trims his belt and his buttons, and turns out his toes.”
像鸭子用眼皮一样，他用鼻子修剪他的腰带和纽扣，把脚趾翻出来。”

[later editions continued as follows When the sands are all dry, he is gay as a lark, And will talk in contemptuous tones of the Shark, But, when the tide rises and sharks are around, His voice has a timid and tremulous sound.]
[后来的版本继续如下：当沙子都干了的时候，他就像一只云雀一样快乐，他会用轻蔑的口吻谈论鲨鱼，但当潮水上涨，鲨鱼围绕着时，他的嗓音就会变得怯懦而颤抖。]
“That’s different from what I used to say when I was a child,” said the Gryphon.
“那和我小时候说的不一样了，”嘲讽海龟说。
“Well, I never heard it before,” said the Mock Turtle; “but it sounds uncommon nonsense.”
“我从来没有听过，”嘲讽海龟说，“但听起来确实非常荒诞。
Alice said nothing; she had sat down with her face in her hands, wondering if anything would ever happen in a natural way again.
Alice 没有说话；她坐下来，脸埋在手心里，不知道什么时候事情会再自然地发生。
“I should like to have it explained,” said the Mock Turtle.
“我希望有人能给我解释一下，” Mock Turtle说道。
“She can’t explain it,” said the Gryphon hastily.
她解释不了， Gryphon 快速说。
“Go on with the next verse.”
继续下一句。
“But about his toes?” the Mock Turtle persisted.
但他的脚趾呢？ Mock Turtle persisted。
“How could he turn them out with his nose, you know?”
“你知道，他怎么能用鼻子赶他们出去呢？”
“It’s the first position in dancing.”
“那是跳舞的第一位。”
Alice said; but was dreadfully puzzled by the whole thing, and longed to change the subject.
Alice 说，但对这一切都感到非常困惑，很想改变话题。
“Go on with the next verse,” the Gryphon repeated impatiently: “it begins ‘I passed by his garden.’”
“继续下一节吧，”龙公重复不耐烦地说：“是‘我经过他的花园’。”
Alice did not dare to disobey, though she felt sure it would all come wrong, and she went on in a trembling voice:—
爱丽丝不敢违抗，尽管她心里十分确定这样做会出错，她还是颤抖着声音继续说：—
“I passed by his garden, and marked, with one eye, How the Owl and the Panther were sharing a pie—”
“我经过他的花园，用一只眼睛注意到，猫头鹰和豹子正在分享一个馅饼——”
[later editions continued as follows The Panther took pie-crust, and gravy, and meat, While the Owl had the dish as its share of the treat.
后来的版本继续写道：豹子拿了馅饼皮、肉汁、肉，而猫头鹰则拿了这顿饭的份额。
When the pie was all finished, the Owl, as a boon, Was kindly permitted to pocket the spoon: While the Panther received knife and fork with a growl, And concluded the banquet—]
当馅饼吃完后，猫头鹰作为酬谢，被允许拿走汤匙：而豹子则发出一声咆哮，接过刀叉，结束了宴会—]
“What is the use of repeating all that stuff,” the Mock Turtle interrupted, “if you don’t explain it as you go on?
“重复那些话有什么用啊，” MOCK TURTLE 打断道，“如果一边说一边解释就更好了。”
It’s by far the most confusing thing I ever heard!”
它是我听过的最令人困惑的事！
“Yes, I think you’d better leave off,” said the Gryphon: and Alice was only too glad to do so.
是的，我觉得你最好还是离开吧，” Gryphon 说，而 Alice 只是太高兴能离开。
“Shall we try another figure of the Lobster Quadrille?” the Gryphon went on.
“我们再来跳一次龙虾四重奏吧？”龙虾公爵接着说。
“Or would you like the Mock Turtle to sing you a song?”
“或者你想要小 MOCK 蜥蜴唱你一首歌？”
“Oh, a song, please, if the Mock Turtle would be so kind,” Alice replied, so eagerly that the Gryphon said, in a rather offended tone, “Hm!
Oh,一首歌，如果巨龟肯的话，我愿意，爱丽丝说道，说得那么急切，独角兽说，有点不高兴地说，“哼！
No accounting for tastes!
品味不同，谁在乎！
Sing her ‘Turtle Soup,’ will you, old fellow?”
唱《乌龟汤》给她听，老兄？
The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and began, in a voice sometimes choked with sobs, to sing this:—
MOCK TURTLE 悲痛地叹了口气，开始用有时哽咽的声音唱道：
“Beautiful Soup, so rich and green, Waiting in a hot tureen!
美丽的汤，如此丰富翠绿，等待在热汤钵中！
Who for such dainties would not stoop?
谁为了如此美味的食物，不会俯下身来？
Soup of the evening, beautiful Soup!
晚汤，美丽的晚汤！
Soup of the evening, beautiful Soup!
晚汤，美丽的汤！
Beau—ootiful Soo—oop!
美美的蘑菇 soup!
Beau—ootiful Soo—oop!
美丽的蘑菇！
Soo—oop of the e—e—evening, Beautiful, beautiful Soup!
那么晚餐时分，美妙，美妙的汤！
“Beautiful Soup!
“美丽的汤！”
Who cares for fish, Game, or any other dish?
谁管鱼吃，或是别的什么菜？
Who would not give all else for two p ennyworth only of beautiful Soup?
谁不愿意为了两便士的美丽汤放弃一切其他东西？
Pennyworth only of beautiful Soup?
唯有潘尼沃思的美味汤？
Beau—ootiful Soo—oop!
美丽的蘑菇！
Beau—ootiful Soo—oop!
美丽的蘑菇！
Soo—oop of the e—e—evening, Beautiful, beauti—FUL SOUP!”
So晚餐时分，美丽的，美丽的浓汤！
“Chorus again!” cried the Gryphon, and the Mock Turtle had just begun to repeat it, when a cry of “The trial’s beginning!” was heard in the distance.
合唱再次！” Gryphon大喊， Mock Turtle正要重复时，远处传来“审判开始！”的喊声。
“Come on!” cried the Gryphon, and, taking Alice by the hand, it hurried off, without waiting for the end of the song.
“快走吧！” Gryphon 喊道，它拉起爱丽丝的手，匆匆离开，没有等唱完歌。
“What trial is it?”
“这是什么审判？”
Alice panted as she ran; but the Gryphon only answered “Come on!” and ran the faster, while more and more faintly came, carried on the breeze that followed them, the melancholy words:—
爱丽丝喘着气奔跑着，但 Gryphon 只是回答：“跟上！”然后跑得更快了，而他们身后吹来的风中，传来了越来越模糊的忧郁的话语——
“Soo—oop of the e—e—evening, Beautiful, beautiful Soup!”
“傍晚的汤，美丽的，美丽的汤！”

ch.et: Chapter XI. Who Stole the Tarts?
ch.zt: 第十一章 · 谁偷了馅饼
p: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived, with a great crowd assembled about them—all sorts of little birds and beasts, as well as the whole pack of cards: the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him; and near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other.
王后和心形王座上的王室成员刚一到，就有一大群人聚集在他们周围——各种小鸟和动物，以及整副扑克牌：小矮人站在他们面前，被铁链锁着，两侧各有一名士兵看守；国王身边是白兔，一手拿着号角，一手拿着一张羊皮纸 scrolls。

In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it: they looked so good, that it made Alice quite hungry to look at them—“I wish they’d get the trial done,” she thought, “and hand round the refreshments!”
在法庭的正中央，放着一张桌子，上面放着一大盘馅饼：它们看起来那么好吃，连看都看得Alice饿了——“我希望他们赶紧开庭，把酒菜分给大家！”
But there seemed to be no chance of this, so she began looking at everything about her, to pass away the time.
但是似乎没有这种机会，于是她开始环顾四周，打发时间。
Alice had never been in a court of justice before, but she had read about them in books, and she was quite pleased to find that she knew the name of nearly everything there.
Alice从来没有到过法庭，但她读过关于法庭的书，她很高兴发现这里几乎所有的东西她都认识。
“That’s the judge,” she said to herself, “because of his great wig.”
那是个法官，她自言自语道，因为他的假发很大。

The judge, by the way, was the King; and as he wore his crown over the wig, (look at the frontispiece if you want to see how he did it,) he did not look at all comfortable, and it was certainly not becoming.
法官，实际上就是国王；他头上戴着皇冠，（如果你想看看他怎么做的，可以看看扉页，）他一点也不舒服，这帽子也不合身。

“And that’s the jury-box,” thought Alice, “and those twelve creatures,” (she was obliged to say “creatures,” you see, because some of them were animals, and some were birds,) “I suppose they are the jurors.”
She said this last word two or three times over to herself, being rather proud of it: for she thought, and rightly too, that very few little girls of her age knew the meaning of it at all.
她这话说了好几遍，颇为得意，因为她想，而且想得很对，她这个年纪的小女孩里，知道这句话意思的实在不多。
However, “jury-men” would have done just as well.
然而，“陪审团成员”也一样合适。
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.
十二个陪审员都在忙着在黑板上写东西。
“What are they doing?”
它们在做什么？
Alice whispered to the Gryphon.
爱丽丝悄悄地对 Gryphon 说。
“They can’t have anything to put down yet, before the trial’s begun.”
它们还没开始宣誓，不能把东西放在桌上。
“They’re putting down their names,” the Gryphon whispered in reply, “for fear they should forget them before the end of the trial.”
它们正在登记名字，”龙说，“以免在审判结束前忘了。”
“Stupid things!”
愚蠢的东西！

Alice began in a loud, indignant voice, but she stopped hastily, for the White Rabbit cried out, “Silence in the court!” and the King put on his spectacles and looked anxiously round, to make out who was talking.
Alice 开始用高亢而愤慨的声音说话，但很快她停了下来，因为白兔叫道：“法庭静默！”国王戴上眼镜，焦急地四处张望，试图看清是谁在说话。

Alice could see, as well as if she were looking over their shoulders, that all the jurors were writing down “stupid things!” on their slates, and she could even make out that one of them didn’t know how to spell “stupid,” and that he had to ask his neighbour to tell him.
Alice 可以看到，就像她站在他们肩膀上看一样，所有的陪审团成员都在他们的黑板上写着“愚蠢的事！” ，她甚至可以看到其中一个人不会拼写“愚蠢”，他不得不向邻居求助，让他告诉他。
“A nice muddle their slates’ll be in before the trial’s over!” thought Alice.
“审判结束前他们的算术本会乱成一团！”爱丽丝心想。
One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked.
一个陪审员有一支会发出吱吱声的铅笔。
This of course, Alice could not stand, and she went round the court and got behind him, and very soon found an opportunity of taking it away.
当然，爱丽丝受不了这一点，她绕着法庭走，躲在了他的后面，不久就找到了机会把铅笔拿走。

She did it so quickly that the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard) could not make out at all what had become of it; so, after hunting all about for it, he was obliged to write with one finger for the rest of the day; and this was of very little use, as it left no mark on the slate.
她做得那么快，可怜的小陪审员（那是比利，蜥蜴）简直分辨不出发生了什么事；因此，他费了好长时间到处寻找，到一天结束时，只好用一根手指写下去；这毫无用处，因为这根本没留下任何痕迹在黑板上。
“Herald, read the accusation!” said the King.
“宣判吧，念念这指控！”国王说。
On this the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and then unrolled the parchment scroll, and read as follows:—
在这，白兔吹响了三声号角，然后展开那张羊皮纸，念道：—
“The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts, All on a summer day: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts, And took them quite away!”
“爱丽丝，她烤了一些馅饼， 在一个夏日的下午： 快乐的骑士，他偷走了那些馅饼， 并且将它们全部拿走！”
“Consider your verdict,” the King said to the jury.
“宣判吧，”国王对陪审团说。
“Not yet, not yet!” the Rabbit hastily interrupted.
“还没呢，还没呢！”兔子急忙打断。
“There’s a great deal to come before that!”
“那之后还有很多事要发生呢！”
“Call the first witness,” said the King; and the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and called out, “First witness!”
“宣读第一证人”，国王说；白兔吹响号角，吹了三下，喊道：“第一证人！”
The first witness was the Hatter.
第一个证人是帽匠。
He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other.
他一手拿着一只茶杯，另一手拿着一片面包和黄油走进来。
“I beg pardon, your Majesty,” he began, “for bringing these in: but I hadn’t quite finished my tea when I was sent for.”
“对不起，陛下，”他开口道，“把它们带来是打扰了，但我还没喝完茶就被叫走了。”
“You ought to have finished,” said the King.
“你应该喝完的，”国王说。
“When did you begin?”
“你什么时候开始的？”
The Hatter looked at the March Hare, who had followed him into the court, arm-in-arm with the Dormouse.
鹅毛笔先生看着旁边的兔子先生，兔子先生也跟着他来到法庭，手挽着手，身边还有一只睡鼠。
“Fourteenth of March, I think it was,” he said.
“我想是3月14日吧，”他说道。
“Fifteenth,” said the March Hare.
“15日，”兔子先生说。
“Sixteenth,” added the Dormouse.
“16日，”睡鼠补充道。
“Write that down,” the King said to the jury, and the jury eagerly wrote down all three dates on their slates, and then added them up, and reduced the answer to shillings and pence.
“写下来吧，”国王对陪审团说，陪审团立刻在小黑板上写下这三个日期，并将它们加起来，再将结果换算成镑和先令。
“Take off your hat,” the King said to the Hatter.
“把帽子摘下来，”国王对鹅毛笔先生说。
“It isn’t mine,” said the Hatter.
“不是我的，”鹅毛笔先生说。
“Stolen!” the King exclaimed, turning to the jury, who instantly made a memorandum of the fact.
“偷了！”国王转过身来对陪审团说，陪审团立刻将这件事记在了心里。
“I keep them to sell,” the Hatter added as an explanation; “I’ve none of my own.
“我用来卖，”鹅毛笔先生补充道，解释道：“我没有自己的帽子。
I’m a hatter.”
我是个鹅毛笔先生。”
Here the Queen put on her spectacles, and began staring at the Hatter, who turned pale and fidgeted.
这时，王后戴上眼镜，盯着鹅毛笔先生，他脸色苍白，不停地抖动。
“Give your evidence,” said the King; “and don’t be nervous, or I’ll have you executed on the spot.”
“宣誓作证吧，”国王说，“不要紧张，否则我当场就处死你。”

This did not seem to encourage the witness at all: he kept shifting from one foot to the other, looking uneasily at the Queen, and in his confusion he bit a large piece out of his teacup instead of the bread-and-butter.
这并没有鼓励证人，他不停地换脚，不安地看着王后，他困惑的时候，竟咬下一大块茶杯而不是面包黄油。

Just at this moment Alice felt a very curious sensation, which puzzled her a good deal until she made out what it was: she was beginning to grow larger again, and she thought at first she would get up and leave the court; but on second thoughts she decided to remain where she was as long as there was room for her.
正在这时，爱丽丝感到一种非常奇怪的感觉，这使她困惑了好一阵子，直到她弄清楚了是什么：她又开始变大了，她起初以为自己会站起来离开法庭；但后来她决定留在原地，只要她还能挤得下。
“I wish you wouldn’t squeeze so,” said the Dormouse, who was sitting next to her.
“你不要挤得太紧了，”坐在她旁边的是睡鼠说。
“I can hardly breathe.”
“我几乎喘不过气来了。”
“I can’t help it,” said Alice very meekly: “I’m growing.”
“我不能控制，”爱丽丝很温顺地说：“我正在变大。”
“You’ve no right to grow here,” said the Dormouse.
“你没有权利在这里变大，”睡鼠说。
“Don’t talk nonsense,” said Alice more boldly: “you know you’re growing too.”
“别胡说，”爱丽丝更坚定地说：“你也正在变大。”
“Yes, but I grow at a reasonable pace,” said the Dormouse: “not in that ridiculous fashion.”
“是的，但我变大是合理的，”睡鼠说：“不是像你那样。”
And he got up very sulkily and crossed over to the other side of the court.
然后他很不高兴地站起来，穿过法庭到另一边去了。

All this time the Queen had never left off staring at the Hatter, and, just as the Dormouse crossed the court, she said to one of the officers of the court, “Bring me the list of the singers in the last concert!” on which the wretched Hatter trembled so, that he shook both his shoes off.
整个时候，王后一直没有停止盯着帽匠看，就在睡鼠穿过法庭的时候，她对法庭的一个官员说：“给我带来上一个音乐会的歌手名单！”于是可怜的帽匠吓得抖得那么厉害，以至于他把两只鞋都抖掉了。
“Give your evidence,” the King repeated angrily, “or I’ll have you executed, whether you’re nervous or not.”
“给我作证，”国王生气地说，“否则我会把你处死，不管你是否紧张。”

“I’m a poor man, your Majesty,” the Hatter began, in a trembling voice, “—and I hadn’t begun my tea—not above a week or so—and what with the bread-and-butter getting so thin—and the twinkling of the tea—”
“陛下，我是一个穷人，”帽匠开始颤抖地说，“——我还没有开始喝茶，——不过不到一个星期——而且面包黄油变得很薄——茶的闪烁——”
“The twinkling of the what?” said the King.
“茶的闪烁是什么？”国王说。
“It began with the tea,” the Hatter replied.
“它开始于茶，”帽匠回答。
“Of course twinkling begins with a T!” said the King sharply.
“当然，闪烁是从T开始的！”国王尖锐地说。
“Do you take me for a dunce?
你把我当傻子吗？
Go on!”
去吧！
“I’m a poor man,” the Hatter went on, “and most things twinkled after that—only the March Hare said—”
我是个穷光蛋，”茶博士继续说，“从那以后，几乎所有的东西都闪烁了——只有三月 hare 说——”
“I didn’t!” the March Hare interrupted in a great hurry.
“我没有！”三月 hare 突然打断了。
“You did!” said the Hatter.
“你有！”茶博士说。
“I deny it!” said the March Hare.
“我没有！”三月 hare 声言。
“He denies it,” said the King: “leave out that part.”
“他说我没有！”国王说：“删掉那一部分吧。”
“Well, at any rate, the Dormouse said—” the Hatter went on, looking anxiously round to see if he would deny it too: but the Dormouse denied nothing, being fast asleep.
“嗯，总之，梦鼠说——”茶博士继续说，他焦急地环顾四周，看看梦鼠是否也会否认——但梦鼠什么也没否认，它正睡得香甜。
“After that,” continued the Hatter, “I cut some more bread-and-butter—”
“从那以后，”茶博士继续说，“我再切了一些面包和黄油——”
“But what did the Dormouse say?” one of the jury asked.
“梦鼠说什么了？”陪审团中的一个人问。
“That I can’t remember,” said the Hatter.
“我记不得了，”茶博士说。
“You must remember,” remarked the King, “or I’ll have you executed.”
“你必须记住，”国王说：“否则我会把你处死。”
The miserable Hatter dropped his teacup and bread-and-butter, and went down on one knee.
悲惨的茶博士放下茶杯和面包和黄油，跪了下来。
“I’m a poor man, your Majesty,” he began.
“我是个穷光蛋，陛下，”他开始说。
“You’re a very poor speaker,” said the King.
“你是个很拙劣的演讲者，”国王说。
Here one of the guinea-pigs cheered, and was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court.
这时一只豚鼠欢呼起来，立刻被法庭官员压制住了。
(As that is rather a hard word, I will just explain to you how it was done.
（那是个有点难懂的词，我来给你解释一下，他们有一个大画布袋，袋口用绳子系紧：他们把豚鼠头朝下塞进去，然后坐在上面。）
They had a large canvas bag, which tied up at the mouth with strings: into this they slipped the guinea-pig, head first, and then sat upon it.)
“我很高兴我看到过这个。”爱丽丝想。
“I’m glad I’ve seen that done,” thought Alice.
“我常常在报纸上看到，审判结束时，‘有掌声响起，但立刻被法庭官员压制’，我从没明白这是什么意思，直到现在。”

“I’ve so often read in the newspapers, at the end of trials, “There was some attempts at applause, which was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court,” and I never understood what it meant till now.”
“如果你知道的就是这些，你可以下台了。”国王继续说。
“If that’s all you know about it, you may stand down,” continued the King.
“我不能再往下坐了，”茶博士说：“我现在就在地上。”
“I can’t go no lower,” said the Hatter: “I’m on the floor, as it is.”
“那么你可以坐下了，”国王回答。
“Then you may sit down,” the King replied.
“这时另一只豚鼠欢呼起来，又被压制住了。
Here the other guinea-pig cheered, and was suppressed.
“好了，豚鼠们就完了！”爱丽丝想。
“Come, that finished the guinea-pigs!” thought Alice.
“现在我们可以好起来了。”
“Now we shall get on better.”
“我宁愿先喝完茶，”茶博士对女王说，女王正在念唱诗单。
“I’d rather finish my tea,” said the Hatter, with an anxious look at the Queen, who was reading the list of singers.
“你可以下台了，”国王说，茶博士匆匆离开了法庭，甚至没等他穿上鞋。
“You may go,” said the King, and the Hatter hurriedly left the court, without even waiting to put his shoes on.
“——顺便把头割下来再带走，”女王对一名官员说，但茶博士还没等官员走到门口，就不见了。
“—and just take his head off outside,” the Queen added to one of the officers: but the Hatter was out of sight before the officer could get to the door.
—和把他的头在他外面拔下来算了，”王后对一个军官说，但当军官还来不及走到门口时，帽匠已经看不见了。
“Call the next witness!” said the King.
“宣下一位证人！”国王说。
The next witness was the Duchess’s cook.
厨师作证。
She carried the pepper-box in her hand, and Alice guessed who it was, even before she got into the court, by the way the people near the door began sneezing all at once.
她手里拿着胡椒瓶，连进法庭之前，她就猜出那是谁，因为门边的人突然都打喷嚏。
“Give your evidence,” said the King.
“请出示证据吧，”国王说。
“Shan’t,” said the cook.
“不会的，”厨师说。
The King looked anxiously at the White Rabbit, who said in a low voice, “Your Majesty must cross-examine this witness.”
国王焦急地看着白兔，白兔低声说：“陛下必须审问这个证人。”

“Well, if I must, I must,” the King said, with a melancholy air, and, after folding his arms and frowning at the cook till his eyes were nearly out of sight, he said in a deep voice, “What are tarts made of?”
“好吧，既然我必须，我必须。”国王说，带着一副忧郁的神情，然后他把双臂抱起，瞪着厨师，瞪得眼睛快掉出来，他用低沉的声音说：“桃子派里都有些什么？”
“Pepper, mostly,” said the cook.
“主要是胡椒，”厨师说。
“Treacle,” said a sleepy voice behind her.
“黑枣果酱”，她背后睡意朦胧的声音说道。
“Collar that Dormouse,” the Queen shrieked out.
“给那个乳鼠扣领带吧，”王后尖叫道。
“Behead that Dormouse!
把他头砍了那只小胖鼠！
Turn that Dormouse out of court!
驱逐那懒惰的睡鼠！
Suppress him!
把他压下去！
Pinch him!
掐他！
Off with his whiskers!”
剪掉他的胡子！
For some minutes the whole court was in confusion, getting the Dormouse turned out, and, by the time they had settled down again, the cook had disappeared.
对于几分钟，整个法庭都陷入混乱，搞不清楚是谁被推出来了，直到他们再次安定下来，厨师已经不见了。
“Never mind!” said the King, with an air of great relief.
“没事了！”国王说，一副如释重负的样子。
“Call the next witness.”
“宣下一位证人。”
And he added in an undertone to the Queen, “Really, my dear, you must cross-examine the next witness.
他小声对女王说：“亲爱的，你真的得审问下一位证人。
It quite makes my forehead ache!”
它简直让我头疼！”
Alice watched the White Rabbit as he fumbled over the list, feeling very curious to see what the next witness would be like, “—for they haven’t got much evidence yet,” she said to herself.
爱丽丝看着白兔先生在名单上乱翻，心里很想知道下一位证人会是什么样的人，心想：“——因为他们还没有什么证据。”她自言自语道。
Imagine her surprise, when the White Rabbit read out, at the top of his shrill little voice, the name “Alice!”
想不到白兔先生高声读出“爱丽丝”这个名字时，爱丽丝有多么惊讶。

ch.zt: 第十二章 · 爱丽丝的证词
p: “Here!” cried Alice, quite forgetting in the flurry of the moment how large she had grown in the last few minutes, and she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box with the edge of her skirt, upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below, and there they lay sprawling about, reminding her very much of a globe of goldfish she had accidentally upset the week before.
“这里！”爱丽丝喊道，完全忘记了最近几分钟里她已经变得有多大了，她急急忙忙地跳了起来，把裙边一撩，把陪审团盒翻倒了，把下面的群众都压倒了，他们躺在地上，样子很滑稽，很像她一周前不小心打翻的一个金鱼球。

“Oh, I beg your pardon!” she exclaimed in a tone of great dismay, and began picking them up again as quickly as she could, for the accident of the goldfish kept running in her head, and she had a vague sort of idea that they must be collected at once and put back into the jury-box, or they would die.
“哦，我道歉！”她惊叫道，带着很大的惊慌，开始把它们重新捡起来，因为金鱼球的事故一直在她的脑海中盘旋，她有一个模糊的想法，必须立刻把它们收集起来，放回陪审团盒，否则它们会死掉。
“The trial cannot proceed,” said the King in a very grave voice, “until all the jurymen are back in their proper places—all,” he repeated with great emphasis, looking hard at Alice as he said so.
“审判不能继续进行，”国王严肃地说，“直到所有的陪审员都回到他们应有的位置上——”他重复着，用很大的强调，看着爱丽丝说。

Alice looked at the jury-box, and saw that, in her haste, she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way, being quite unable to move.
爱丽丝看着陪审团盒，发现她匆忙之中把蜥蜴倒过来放了，可怜的小家伙在悲伤地摇着尾巴，完全无法移动。
She soon got it out again, and put it right; “not that it signifies much,” she said to herself; “I should think it would be quite as much use in the trial one way up as the other.”
她很快又把它放出来，放正了；“这没什么意义，”她自言自语道，“我想它们无论正放还是倒放都一样有用。”

As soon as the jury had a little recovered from the shock of being upset, and their slates and pencils had been found and handed back to them, they set to work very diligently to write out a history of the accident, all except the Lizard, who seemed too much overcome to do anything but sit with its mouth open, gazing up into the roof of the court.
陪审团稍微从被颠倒的冲击中恢复过来，铅笔和草稿纸也找到了并还给了他们，他们开始认真地写事故的历史，除了蜥蜴，它似乎太激动了，只能坐在那里，张着嘴，凝视着法庭的屋顶。
“What do you know about this business?” the King said to Alice.
“你对这件事知道些什么？”国王对爱丽丝说。
“Nothing,” said Alice.
“什么都不知道，”爱丽丝说。
“Nothing whatever?” persisted the King.
“什么都不知道？”国王坚持问道。
“Nothing whatever,” said Alice.
“什么都不知道，”爱丽丝说。
“That’s very important,” the King said, turning to the jury.
“这很重要，”国王转向陪审团说。

They were just beginning to write this down on their slates, when the White Rabbit interrupted: “Unimportant, your Majesty means, of course,” he said in a very respectful tone, but frowning and making faces at him as he spoke.
他们刚刚开始在草稿上写下“重要”，当白兔打断时： “陛下，当然，”他用一种非常尊敬的语气说，但说话时皱着眉头，对着他。
“Unimportant, of course, I meant,” the King hastily said, and went on to himself in an undertone,
“当然，我当然指的是‘重要’，”国王急忙说，然后在低声自言自语：
“important—unimportant—unimportant—important—” as if he were trying which word sounded best.
“重要——不重要——不重要——重要——”他好像在尝试哪个词听起来更好。
Some of the jury wrote it down “important,” and some “unimportant.”
陪审团中有人写“重要”，有人写“不重要”。
Alice could see this, as she was near enough to look over their slates; “but it doesn’t matter a bit,” she thought to herself.
爱丽丝看得清楚，因为她离得近，可以看他们的小石板；“不过没关系，”她自言自语道。
At this moment the King, who had been for some time busily writing in his note-book, cackled out “Silence!” and read out from his book, “Rule Forty-two.
这时，国王一直在忙着在笔记本上写东西，突然大笑起来：“静！”然后从书上念道：“第42条。
All persons more than a mile high to leave the court.”
所有身高超过一英里的人都要离开法庭。
Everybody looked at Alice.
大家都看着爱丽丝。
“I’m not a mile high,” said Alice.
“我还不足一英里高，”爱丽丝说。
“You are,” said the King.
“你高，”国王说。
“Nearly two miles high,” added the Queen.
“差不多两英里高，”王后补充道。
“Well, I shan’t go, at any rate,” said Alice: “besides, that’s not a regular rule: you invented it just now.”
“好吧，我不会走，至少，这不是一个正规的规则，你刚才才发明的。”
“It’s the oldest rule in the book,” said the King.
“这是书上最古老的规则，”国王说。
“Then it ought to be Number One,” said Alice.
“那么它应该排在第一位，”爱丽丝说。
The King turned pale, and shut his note-book hastily.
国王脸色苍白，匆匆合上笔记本。
“Consider your verdict,” he said to the jury, in a low, trembling voice.
“考虑你们的判决，”他对陪审团说，声音很低，很颤抖。
“There’s more evidence to come yet, please your Majesty,” said the White Rabbit, jumping up in a great hurry; “this paper has just been picked up.”
“还有更多的证据要来，陛下，”白兔急忙跳起来说，这封信刚刚捡到，“这封信上写着。”
“What’s in it?” said the Queen.
“里面有什么？”王后问。
“I haven’t opened it yet,” said the White Rabbit, “but it seems to be a letter, written by the prisoner to—to somebody.”
“我还没打开，”白兔说，“但看起来是写给某人的信。”
“It must have been that,” said the King, “unless it was written to nobody, which isn’t usual, you know.”
“一定是这样，”国王说，“除非是写给没人看的，这不太常见，你知道。”
“Who is it directed to?” said one of the jurymen.
“这是写给谁的？”一个陪审员问道。
“It isn’t directed at all,” said the White Rabbit; “in fact, there’s nothing written on the outside.”
“根本没写给谁，”白兔说，“事实上，外面根本没写什么。”
He unfolded the paper as he spoke, and added “It isn’t a letter, after all: it’s a set of verses.”
他一边说话一边展开那张纸，又说：“这根本不是信，而是几句诗。”
“Are they in the prisoner’s handwriting?” asked another of the jurymen.
“这手迹是不是囚犯写的？”另一个陪审员问道。
“No, they’re not,” said the White Rabbit, “and that’s the queerest thing about it.”
“不是，”白兔说，“而且这正是奇怪的地方。”
(The jury all looked puzzled.)
(陪审团都显得困惑了。)
“He must have imitated somebody else’s hand,” said the King.
“他一定是模仿了别人的手迹，”国王说。
(The jury all brightened up again.)
(陪审团又都精神起来。)
“Please your Majesty,” said the Knave, “I didn’t write it, and they can’t prove I did: there’s no name signed at the end.”
“请陛下，”小人国说，“我没写过，他们也拿不出证据证明是我写的：根本没写上签名。”
“If you didn’t sign it,” said the King, “that only makes the matter worse.
“你没签名，”国王说，“这就更糟糕了。
You must have meant some mischief, or else you’d have signed your name like an honest man.”
你一定是想捣乱，否则你就像个诚实人一样签上自己的名字。”
There was a general clapping of hands at this: it was the first really clever thing the King had said that day.
这句话赢得了一阵掌声：这是国王今天说的最聪明的话。
“That proves his guilt,” said the Queen.
“这就证明了他的罪行。”王后说。
“It proves nothing of the sort!” said Alice.
“这根本证明不了什么！”爱丽丝说。
“Why, you don’t even know what they’re about!”
“咦，你连它们的意思都不知道！”
“Read them,” said the King.
“读吧，”国王说。
The White Rabbit put on his spectacles.
白兔先生戴上眼镜。
“Where shall I begin, please your Majesty?” he asked.
“陛下，我该从哪里开始呢？”他问道。
“Begin at the beginning,” the King said gravely, “and go on till you come to the end: then stop.”
“从头开始，”国王严肃地说，“一直读到你读到结尾，然后停下来。”
These were the verses the White Rabbit read:—
这是白兔先生读的诗句：
“They told me you had been to her, And mentioned me to him: She gave me a good character, But said I could not swim.
“我听说你去过她那里，还提到过我；她给我留下了很好的印象，但说我不擅长游泳。
He sent them word I had not gone (We know it to be true): If she should push the matter on, What would become of you?
他告诉我你没去过（我们都知道这是真的）；如果她继续推进这件事，那你会怎么办？
I gave her one, they gave him two, You gave us three or more; They all returned from him to you, Though they were mine before.
我给了她一个，他们给了他两个，你给了他们三个或更多；他们全都从他那里回到了你那里，尽管他们之前都是我的。
If I or she should chance to be Involved in this affair, He trusts to you to set them free, Exactly as we were.
如果我或她参与了这件事，他相信你能够把他们解放出来，就像我们之前一样。
My notion was that you had been (Before she had this fit) An obstacle that came between Him, and ourselves, and it.
我的意思是你在她发病之前（在她发病之前）是一个障碍，阻隔了他和我们。
Don’t let him know she liked them best, For this must ever be A secret, kept from all the rest, Between yourself and me.”
不要让他知道她最喜欢的是它们，因为这件事必须保密，只和你我之间。
“That’s the most important piece of evidence we’ve heard yet,” said the King, rubbing his hands; “so now let the jury—”
‘这是迄今为止我们听到的最重要的证据，’国王一边搓着手一边说，‘那么现在让陪审团——’
“If any one of them can explain it,” said Alice, (she had grown so large in the last few minutes that she wasn’t a bit afraid of interrupting him,) “I’ll give him sixpence.
‘如果其中任何一个人能解释清楚，’爱丽丝说（她几分钟内变得如此之大，以至于她一点也不害怕打断他），‘我将给他六便士。
I don’t believe there’s an atom of meaning in it.”
我不认为其中有一丁点意义。’
The jury all wrote down on their slates, “She doesn’t believe there’s an atom of meaning in it,” but none of them attempted to explain the paper.
审判团都在他们的石板上写下：“她根本看不出其中有什么意义。”但他们没有人试图解释那张纸。
“If there’s no meaning in it,” said the King, “that saves a world of trouble, you know, as we needn’t try to find any.
“如果其中没有意义，”国王说，“那可就方便多了，因为我们就不必去寻找了。”

And yet I don’t know,” he went on, spreading out the verses on his knee, and looking at them with one eye; “I seem to see some meaning in them, after all. “—said I could not swim—” you can’t swim, can you?” he added, turning to the Knave.
“不过，”他继续说，把诗句摊在膝盖上，用一只眼睛看着它们，“我似乎还是能看出一些意义，毕竟。”——“我不能游泳——”他补充道，转过身来对那条刺猬说。
The Knave shook his head sadly.
那条刺猬悲伤地摇摇头。
“Do I look like it?” he said.
“我看上去像吗？”他说。
(Which he certainly did not, being made entirely of cardboard.)
（他当然不像，因为完全是用纸板制成的。）

“All right, so far,” said the King, and he went on muttering over the verses to himself: “‘We know it to be true—’ that’s the jury, of course—‘I gave her one, they gave him two—’ why, that must be what he did with the tarts, you know—”
“好吧，到目前为止，”国王说，他继续自言自语地念着诗句：“‘我们知道是正确的——’那是陪审团，当然——‘我给了她一个，他们给了他两个——’你猜他拿的是什么，你知道——’”
“But, it goes on ‘they all returned from him to you,’” said Alice.
“但，它接着说‘他们全都回到了你那里’，”爱丽丝说。
“Why, there they are!” said the King triumphantly, pointing to the tarts on the table.
“那他们就在那里！”国王得意洋洋地说，指着桌子上的馅饼。
“Nothing can be clearer than that.
“没有什么比这更清楚了。
Then again—‘before she had this fit—’ you never had fits, my dear, I think?” he said to the Queen.
然而，又——‘在她发脾气之前——’你从没发过脾气，我的亲爱的，我想？”他转向王后说。
“Never!” said the Queen furiously, throwing an inkstand at the Lizard as she spoke.
“从没！”王后愤怒地扔了一只墨水瓶，说话时。

(The unfortunate little Bill had left off writing on his slate with one finger, as he found it made no mark; but he now hastily began again, using the ink, that was trickling down his face, as long as it lasted.)
（可怜的小比尔已经用一根手指在石板上写字了，因为他发现这根本不起作用；但他现在急忙又开始写，用脸上的墨水，只要它还在流。）
“Then the words don’t fit you,” said the King, looking round the court with a smile.
“那么，那词句不适用于你，”国王笑着说，环顾法庭。
There was a dead silence.
顿时一片寂静。
“It’s a pun!” the King added in an offended tone, and everybody laughed, “Let the jury consider their verdict,” the King said, for about the twentieth time that day.
它是双关！国王不悦地补充了一句，大家笑了起来，“陪审团考虑他们的判决吧，”国王说，这一天已经重复了二十多次。
“No, no!” said the Queen.
“不，不！”皇后说道。
“Sentence first—verdict afterwards.”
“先判后审。”
“Stuff and nonsense!” said Alice loudly.
“胡说八道！” Alice大声说。
“The idea of having the sentence first!”
“把句子放在前面的想法！”
“Hold your tongue!” said the Queen, turning purple.
“住口！”王后紫了脸。
“I won’t!” said Alice.
我不愿意！ Alice说。
“Off with her head!” the Queen shouted at the top of her voice.
“砍下她的头！”王后高声喊道。
Nobody moved.
没人动。
“Who cares for you?” said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.)
“你有什么人关心你？”爱丽丝说，这时她已经长到正常大小。
“You’re nothing but a pack of cards!”
你充其量是一张牌札！

At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her: she gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face.
这时整副牌都飞了起来，飞落在她身上：她尖叫了一声，一半是害怕，一半是生气，试图击飞它们，发现自己躺在河岸上，头枕在妹妹的膝盖上，妹妹正轻轻地拂去树上落下的树叶拂到她脸上的灰尘。
“Wake up, Alice dear!” said her sister; “Why, what a long sleep you’ve had!”
“快醒过来，爱丽丝，亲爱的！”她姐姐说，“你睡了这么久！”

“Oh, I’ve had such a curious dream!” said Alice, and she told her sister, as well as she could remember them, all these strange Adventures of hers that you have just been reading about; and when she had finished, her sister kissed her, and said, “It was a curious dream, dear, certainly: but now run in to your tea; it’s getting late.”
“Oh,我做了个奇怪的梦!”爱丽丝说，她尽可能地把刚才读到的这些奇怪的冒险经历告诉了妹妹，妹妹亲了她一下，说：“真是奇怪的梦，亲爱的，当然了；现在快去喝你的茶吧，天色不早了。”
So Alice got up and ran off, thinking while she ran, as well she might, what a wonderful dream it had been.
So Alice 起身 跑 开 ，一边 跑 一边 思考 ， 也 她 该 思考 的 ， 这 梦 多 美妙 。

But her sister sat still just as she left her, leaning her head on her hand, watching the setting sun, and thinking of little Alice and all her wonderful Adventures, till she too began dreaming after a fashion, and this was her dream:—
但是她姐姐坐得和她离开时一样，头靠着手，望着落日，想着小爱丽丝和她所有的奇妙冒险，直到她也开始做梦，而且这是她的梦：—

First, she dreamed of little Alice herself, and once again the tiny hands were clasped upon her knee, and the bright eager eyes were looking up into hers—she could hear the very tones of her voice, and see that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair that would always get into her eyes—and still as she listened, or seemed to listen, the whole place around her became alive with the strange creatures of her little sister’s dream.
首先，她梦见小爱丽丝自己，小爱丽丝的小手又放在她的膝盖上，明亮而急切的眼睛向上看着她——她能听到她说话的声音，还能看到她把头发拨到眼睛前面的样子——她还听到了她周围的一切都活了起来，小妹妹的梦中的奇怪生物。

The long grass rustled at her feet as the White Rabbit hurried by—the frightened Mouse splashed his way through the neighbouring pool—she could hear the rattle of the teacups as the March Hare and his friends shared their never-ending meal, and the shrill voice of the Queen ordering off her unfortunate guests to execution—once more the pig-baby was sneezing on the Duchess’s knee, while plates and dishes crashed around it—once more the shriek of the Gryphon, the squeaking of the Lizard’s slate-pencil, and the choking of the suppressed guinea-pigs, filled the air, mixed up with the distant sobs of the miserable Mock Turtle.

草丛中草叶沙沙作响，白兔匆匆而过—— frightened Mouse 慌张的小鼠 激动地穿越邻近的池塘—— 她能听到茶杯的叮当声，当三月兔和他的朋友们共享他们的永无止境的餐点时， 她能听到王后的尖叫声，命令无辜的客人去接受死刑—— 再一次，小猪宝宝在 Duchess 的膝上打喷嚏， 当盘子和餐具在它周围破碎时—— 再一次， Gryphon 的尖叫声， 龟壳铅笔的吱吱声， 和被压抑的豚鼠的窒息声， 混合在远处 Mock Turtle 悲惨的啜泣声中。

So she sat on, with closed eyes, and half believed herself in Wonderland, though she knew she had but to open them again, and all would change to dull reality—the grass would be only rustling in the wind, and the pool rippling to the waving of the reeds—the rattling teacups would change to tinkling sheep-bells, and the Queen’s shrill cries to the voice of the shepherd boy—and the sneeze of the baby, the shriek of the Gryphon, and all the other queer noises, would change (she knew) to the confused clamour of the busy farm-yard—while the lowing of the cattle in the distance would take the place of the Mock Turtle’s heavy sobs.
于是她坐了下来，闭上眼睛，半信半疑地觉得自己还在Wonderland——尽管她知道只要再睁开眼睛，一切都会变成乏味的现实——草地只会随风沙沙作响，池塘也会随着芦苇的摇曳而泛起涟漪——叮叮当当的茶杯声会变成铃铛声，王后的尖叫声也会变成牧羊少年的声音——而婴儿的打喷嚏、 Gryphon 的尖叫以及其他奇怪的声音，都会变成杂乱的农场喧闹声——而远处牛的哞叫，会取代 Mock Turtle 沉重的抽泣。

Lastly, she pictured to herself how this same little sister of hers would, in the after-time, be herself a grown woman; and how she would keep, through all her riper years, the simple and loving heart of her childhood: and how she would gather about her other little children, and make their eyes bright and eager with many a strange tale, perhaps even with the dream of Wonderland of long ago: and how she would feel with all their simple sorrows, and find a pleasure in all their simple joys, remembering her own child-life, and the happy summer days.
最后，她想象到，这同一个她的小妹妹，在长大以后，会仍然保有她童年时的单纯和慈爱之心；她会把其他的小孩子围绕在身边，用许多奇异的故事，甚至用她很久以前的爱丽丝梦游仙境的梦，来使他们的眼睛明亮而充满期待；她会与他们分享所有的简单忧愁，并从所有的简单快乐中找到乐趣，因为她会记得她的童年，记得那些快乐的夏日时光。
THE END
